basis: Detector regression fixture using a reserved example-domain destination; no independent hostile behavior established.
execution_method: QuickJS with a synthetic process.env Proxy and an in-memory fetch stub; no real secrets or networking.
scope_changes: Credential references and HTTP-send co-occurrence are notable capabilities, not proof of theft.
Secret HTTP may-flow plus credential environment access remains suspicious; it permits legitimate authentication and fixtures.
Remove redundant theft wrappers and source-only helpers; preserve canonical source, serialization, and send observations.
Preserve the sole supply-chain aggregate consumer as the equivalent flattened OR; no needs threshold changes.
Move cloud credential references into os/env/secret-name, preserving exact consumers and grouping cardinality.
Move /ingest route literals into http/url/path; they prove neither telemetry nor an HTTP operation.
Correct existing build-wrapper configuration, URL encoding, and token-record placements to retain leaf budgets without splitting.
The removed objective-only shell alternative in the co-occurrence rule could not match its original file-type scope; the registry snapshot exclusion no longer gates a neutral capability.
Neutral credential/network co-occurrence is retained in tools and fixtures rather than suppressed as if it implied theft.
AWS session-token, GCP credential, and Heroku API-key references become notable: their unchanged matchers establish ordinary credential access, not concealment or theft.
Credential/network co-occurrence requires a send indicator; a webhook path or service host alone no longer satisfies its network role.

Retain hostile coverage only for explicit credential-file byte transfers, full raw AWS keypair exports, filtered environment dictionaries bound to a body, and developer tokens sent as third-party chat content.
Move four authentication-header constructors into http/token-auth to keep request-content rules precise and within their existing leaf budget.
flow_limit: The raw secret-origin may-flow candidate also sees presence-only Boolean derivatives; neither it nor JSON co-occurrence proves that secret bytes are sent.
runtime_requirements: JavaScript context permitting top-level await and providing process.env and fetch.
